title: The December 1969 Manassas album
summary: Fat Cat tapes everything; she appeared with two groups and was working with Bobby Hackett in Boston when the album came out.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I just want to mention the title of the album that we've just been discussing, which is on the Fat Cat label, SCJ136,-- The title is a very appropriate one. It's "Maxine Sullivan, Queen of Song." And it has a delightful picture of you on the cover, too.
Next, we come to your appearance at the December 1969 Manassas Festival. Here again, you appear with two groups.
Yeah. Well, as I said before, Fat Cat has a way of taping everything, and then later on when he puts out the album, you don't know what's going to be on it. But --

Well, sometimes that has good results.

Well, I was appearing with Bobby Hackett up in Boston when this album came out. And it came as a surprise to all of us, because we didn't know that Fat Cat was going to put it out. I don't really like to say this, but, I think that Fat Cat in the beginning, he would bring the musicians down there -- of course, they agreed to make the album before it could be taped -- and since that time, he's put out quite a few tapes. I would think a tape -- I mean albums -- he probably has a mailing list and he probably does this through sort of an assembly membership arrangement. But I noticed that a lot of these things have appeared on the market. So, he's in business now, you know.
